findings.text: §22 says `_misfiled_review_candidates`'s 22% is "the per-run stat and lookup work around the cached index, not a fresh listing", but the cited profile attributes that 22% to the cache-missing update pass: of the 302 main-thread samples in `post-landing-profile-75s.raw`, 67 (22.2%) sit under `_misfiled_review_candidates`, and 46 of those 67 sit at `path.stat()` inside `_store_indexes`'s update branch (`review_records.py:1361`), 6 more in the `sorted(directory.glob("*.json"))` that begins that walk (`review_records.py:1356`), and 10 in `_persist_store_entries` that the same miss triggers. That branch runs only after the directory's stat identity has moved and itself performs one `glob` listing plus a stat of every record file, so the measured cost is a fresh listing and a full stat walk, not cheap lookup around a warm cache — the cache-hit path would have shown the leaf in `_store_directory_identity`'s `directory.stat()` instead, and it does not appear.
